To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the position of the ectopically eruptive canine is best determined by a periapical radiograph, but that the resorption of the lateral incisors is best seen on a panoramic film.
2.8% of 10- to 15-year-olds need radiographic examinations for determining the position of the maxillary canine.

1) the radiographs of 3,300 children showed that 7% of the children needed radiographic examination to determine the position of maxillary canine teeth, 2) in the 125 cases of ectopic maxillary canines that were examined, the periapical radiograph was the best diagnostic tool, 3) in 37% the lateral incisor was projected free from the canine, 4) in 29% the lateral incisors were neither projected free
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiographic investigation of ectopically erupted maxillary canines, the need for and usefulness of different radiographic procedures.
the radiological diagnosis and treatment planning in cases of ectopically erupted maxillary canines.
the need for and the possibility of obtaining further radiological information in 84 children with potential ectopically erupted canines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiographic examination is necessary in 3% of the children and that a supplementary polytomography should be considered in about 1%.

a radiographic examination is indicated in cases of ectopically erupted maxillary canines and that the radiographic examination should include both periapical and polytomographic radiographs in all cases.
7% of the 10-15-year-old children need radiographs to determine whether the canines are erupting normally or not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the clinical examination is sufficient for the diagnosis of the position of the ectopically eruptive maxillary canines in most cases.
the clinical and radiographic diagnosis of ectopic eruption is a difficult and time-consuming procedure, but that it is possible to obtain sufficient information for planning the treatment.

in 92% (116) of the 125 potential ectopic canines the position could be judged from conventional periapicals, but in 37% (46) of the 124 canines, the adjacent lateral incisor could not be projected free from resorptive lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiographic examination of the ectopic canine and the adjacent teeth is important for the orthodontic diagnosis, treatment planning and the prognosis of the case.
radiographic examinations of ectopically positioned maxillary canines are needed in a limited number of cases, but when needed, they can be optimized by a stepwise procedure.
the use of a stepwise diagnostic procedure is necessary for a correct diagnosis and treatment planning.
